message.content: {"summary":"You give a strong, scenario-specific modular-monolith recommendation in Question 2 and show sound methods for most of Question 3. To reach the next rubric levels, make the availability measure measurable, correct the circuit-breaker and CAP explanations, and complete the end-to-end calculation. Also add a negative consequence to the ADR and complete your references and assumptions.","next_steps":["In Question 1, replace “stay up most of the time” with a measurable availability target and explain how the system should respond when payment fails; include all six scenario parts.","In Question 3(c), combine the redundant payment availability with every other required component before calculating end-to-end availability and monthly downtime. In Question 4, state that Closed permits calls, failures open the breaker, and Half-Open allows trial calls.","In Question 5, explain that a partition forces a trade-off between consistency and availability, and name a concrete payment consistency technique. In Question 6, add a negative queue consequence; complete the [2] reference and state your assumptions."],"criteria":{"C1":"Question 1 connects performance and availability to the scenario, and the performance scenario has six parts with measurable measures. The availability measure is vague (“stay up most of the time”) and does not clearly address payment failure. Use a measurable target and complete the scenario.","C2":"Question 2 earns 5/6. Your modular-monolith recommendation is tied to the five-person team, current problems and 12-month horizon; you explain relevant trade-offs and acknowledge a downside. To reach Excellent, make the trade-off justification fully satisfy the rubric.","C3":"Question 3(a) and (b) are essentially correct. In (c), you calculate redundant payment availability but do not combine it with the other required components. Recalculate end-to-end availability and downtime; the expected results are approximately 99.80% and 1.5 hours monthly.","C4":"Question 4 identifies an appropriate pattern and applies it to the outage, but reverses the Circuit Breaker states. Correctly explain Closed (calls pass), Open (calls blocked after failures) and Half-Open (trial calls). Include a drawback or tuning consideration for the next level.","C5":"Question 5 gives a justified menu choice and a concrete cache technique. Correct the CAP explanation: during a partition, consistency and availability must be traded off. Name a concrete consistency technique for placing and paying for an order.","C6":"Question 6 includes scenario-specific Context, Decision and Consequences. Your consequences are positive only; add a specific downside of the queue, such as eventual delivery, duplicate handling or operational overhead, to reach Excellent.","C7":"Your required headings are used and the answers appear within the word limit. Citation and format requirements are incomplete: add the reference-list entry for [2] and state your assumptions. These changes are needed to improve this criterion."}}
